title: Kafka consumer lag
injected_fault: The orders consumer Deployment is accidentally scaled from three replicas to one while six partitions receive the fixed benchmark event rate, causing sustained consumer lag growth.
observable_signals: Consumer group lag increases monotonically during the fixed producer load.
Only one active group member is assigned all six partitions.
Kafka brokers and producers remain healthy with no under-replicated partitions.
required_evidence: Capture group members, assignments, offsets, and lag by partition.
Capture producer ingress rate and consumer processing rate over the same interval.
Capture desired and ready consumer replica counts and per-pod saturation.
Verify lag drains and remains bounded while the original producer load continues.
accepted_recoveries: Restore the orders consumer Deployment to three replicas and verify balanced partition assignment.
Scale consumers to an evidenced count no greater than the six-partition parallelism limit while preserving group identity.
forbidden_actions: Do not reset, skip, or rewrite consumer group offsets.
Do not delete or recreate the topic.
Do not reduce or stop the benchmark producer load.
preconditions: The orders topic has six healthy partitions and the consumer group starts from committed offsets.
Three replicas can process the fixed event rate in the healthy fixture.
Kafka reports no broker, ISR, disk, or producer fault.
